name: Should You Repair or Replace a Damaged Driveway?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace the whole driveway, or can a driveway contractor repair only the damaged section?
mainEntity.text: Do I need to replace the whole driveway, or can a driveway contractor repair only the damaged section?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial repair makes sense when the damage is limited to one area, such as a cracked panel, a settled edge, or a small section affected by a tree root or vehicle impact. Full replacement is usually the better choice when there are widespread cracks, repeated settlement, crumbling edges, or drainage issues that will keep damaging the surface. A contractor should inspect the base, not just the visible top layer, because surface patching will not fix a failed foundation. In Los Angeles County, homeowners also need to consider whether a repair will blend with the rest of the driveway. Older concrete, pavers, or asphalt often differ in color and texture after repair. A good contractor will explain whether a patch, overlay, slab replacement, or full rebuild is the most durable option. If the problem is isolated and the base is stable, a targeted repair can save money. If the driveway has multiple failure points, full replacement usually delivers better long-term value.
acceptedAnswer.description: A driveway contractor can often repair only the damaged section if the rest of the driveway is structurally sound and the failure is localized. Full replacement is more likely when there is widespread cracking, sinking, poor base support, or drainage problems. Matching the old finish and color may be difficult, so partial repair is best when appearance differences are acceptable.
